# KBD constraints — prometheus-skills-mini

Generated by `/kbd-init` on 2026-09-21; command fields regenerated by `/kbd-init --force` on
2026-09-21 after `project-scaffold` and `platform-spawn` landed. That regeneration is kbd-init's
own job, not a change editing its gates — the ownership table below distinguishes the two. The
`openspec validate …` form it replaced could never have run on Windows: npm installs the CLI as
`openspec.cmd`, which Node cannot start without a shell. `AGENTS.md` has no "Never Do" section, so the blocking rules are
derived from its §P project block and §A constitution, and from the hard constraints in
`openspec/config.yaml`. Each rule names its source.

## Command policy (applies to every `check:`, `command:` and `target:` below)

This project forbids telling an agent to run `grep`, `sed`, `jq`, `awk`, `curl`, `mktemp` or `chmod`, and
requires every command to behave the same from `cmd.exe`, Windows PowerShell 5.1, bash and zsh. So:

- Content checks use **`git grep --no-index --exclude-standard`** — `git` is a permitted dependency, it is a
  native Windows executable, and `--no-index` works whether or not the directory is a git repository.
  Pathspecs such as `"lib/*.mjs"` are recursive. **A match is a violation**: exit 0 = violations printed,
  exit 1 = clean.
- Double quotes only. No `&&`, `||` or `;` chaining — Windows PowerShell 5.1 rejects `&&`. Steps that must run
  in sequence are separate entries.
- `[$]` stands for a literal dollar sign so the pattern means the same thing inside and outside a POSIX shell.
- Every check below was run against known-bad fixtures at generation time and matched exactly the intended
  lines. No mandatory command wrapper, toolchain selector or external storage path is declared by this
  project, so there is no prefix to propagate. If a `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` policy is ever adopted, it must be
  added to every compiling command here.

## Path ownership — hidden does not mean disposable

| Path | Owner | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/`, `.cursor/rules/`, `docs/skill-routing.md` | `rules/build.mjs` | Generated. Edit `rules/src/`, then rebuild. A hand edit fails `build-passes`. |
| `.claude/skills/openspec-*`, `.claude/commands/opsx/`, `.agents/skills/openspec-*`, `.cursor/commands/`, `.cursor/skills/`, `.opencode/` | OpenSpec CLI | Refresh with `openspec update`; do not hand-edit. |
| `.kbd-orchestrator/project.json` — everything except `activePhase` | `/kbd-init` ONLY | Never written by a change. Command fields are derived from `package.json` scripts; re-run `/kbd-init --force` after they change. |
| `.kbd-orchestrator/project.json` — `activePhase` | `/kbd-new-phase`, `/kbd-next-phase` | Step 7 of those skills flips it at a phase bracket. Under runtime authority the runtime projects the waypoint and the phase directory but NOT this field, so the skill still writes it. A change never touches it. |
| `.kbd-orchestrator/constraints.md` — rules and thresholds | `/kbd-init` | A change never loosens, deletes or adds a RULE here. |
| `.kbd-orchestrator/constraints.md` — a `check:` expression | a change, with evidence | Permitted ONLY to fix a demonstrated false positive, and only when the change ALSO proves the corrected check still catches a real violation. Every such edit is called out in its own commit and in the change's tasks. Three exist (see below); each was a check matching prose rather than code. |
| `.kbd-orchestrator/phases/**` | KBD stages | Written by the stage that owns them. |
| `.prometheus/` | Karpathy logging / memory | Append-only and dated. Entries are marked superseded, never deleted. |
| `openspec/changes/archive/` | OpenSpec | History. Never rewritten. |
| `/Users/gqadonis/Projects/prometheus/prometheus-skill-pack` | another repository | Reference only (`project.json` → `workspace`). **Never written**, including its worktrees. |

### Check expressions corrected by a change

| Constraint | False positive it matched | Proof it still discriminates |
|---|---|---|
| `no-home-or-tmp-literals` | a comment in `lib/platform/paths.mjs` naming `$HOME` while explaining the rule | `process.env.HOME` added to a code line is reported |
| (reverted) `no-home-or-tmp-literals` v2 | — | a `grep` pipe was used, which this project forbids and Windows lacks; reverted to the plain form |
| (reverted) `os-locations-only-via-platform` | — | a TIGHTENING, not a loosening: the check reported clean over four real `scripts/` violations. The corrected pattern was verified by execution, but applying it required a rule authorising check tightenings, and a change writing its own authorisation is the same circularity as widening a gate to fit its own code. Reverted; the false negative is documented in the constraint's `note:` and left for the rule owner |

One correction remains (`no-home-or-tmp-literals`), and it is not circular: the text it excuses is a
COMMENT IN THE RULE'S OWN SUBJECT — `lib/platform/paths.mjs` cannot explain why nothing else may read
a home location without naming what it forbids. A second correction was reverted after review pointed
out the circularity: a test fixture had tripped `no-console-log-in-lib`, and widening the check to
excuse it was loosening a gate to fit my own code. The fixture was changed instead, and the original
check restored. That is the standard: change the code, not the gate.

---

## Blocking constraints (prevent archiving until resolved)

```yaml
constraints:
  - id: build-passes
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md pointer block; openspec/config.yaml (rules v4)'
    description: 'Generated agent rules match rules/src/ and stay inside the Layer 0 / Layer 1 budgets'
    command: 'npm run check'

  - id: tests-pass
    severity: blocking
    source: 'openspec/config.yaml conventions'
    description: 'The node:test suite passes'
    command: 'npm test'

  - id: specs-valid
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — OpenSpec is the spec backend'
    description: 'All OpenSpec specs and active changes validate'
    command: 'npm run spec:validate'

  - id: no-shell-or-python-files
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — Node.js LTS is the only script runtime'
    description: 'No .sh, .bash, .py or .ps1 file anywhere in the repository'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -l -e "" -- "*.sh" "*.bash" "*.py" "*.ps1" ":!tools/prometheus-knowledge"'
    note: 'One pathspec exclusion, added 2026-09-21 when the operator directed that the Rust pk CLI be vendored as a submodule at tools/prometheus-knowledge: that repository carries scripts/pk-lint-cron.sh and scripts/pmpo-reflect.sh. They are upstream files this project neither authors nor runs, and --no-index scans the working tree, so without the exclusion a vendored checkout fails a rule about what THIS project ships. The pattern is unchanged; proof it still discriminates: a .sh created anywhere else, including directly under tools/, is reported. A .ps1 is admissible only beside a cross-platform equivalent, and only through an OpenSpec change that says why Node cannot do the job. Then scope this check; do not delete it.'

  - id: no-shell-true
    severity: blocking
    source: '.claude/rules/node-scripts.md — Processes'
    description: 'Child processes are spawned with shell: false and an args array'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "shell: *true" -- "lib/*.mjs" "scripts/*.mjs" "hooks/*.mjs" "rules/*.mjs"'

  - id: no-home-or-tmp-literals
    severity: blocking
    source: '.claude/rules/node-scripts.md — Paths'
    description: 'Paths come from os.homedir() / os.tmpdir() / path.join, never $HOME, process.env.HOME or /tmp'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "[$]HOME|process\.env\.HOME|/tmp/" -- "lib/*.mjs" "scripts/*.mjs" "hooks/*.mjs" "rules/*.mjs"'
    note: 'Back to the original -E form, with no pipe and no PCRE. An earlier attempt to exempt comments used a grep pipe (forbidden by the command policy, and grep is absent on stock Windows) and then git grep -P (PCRE is a build-time option, so the check could error on another machine). Neither is needed: the comment that triggered this now describes the forbidden spellings instead of quoting them, so the plain check passes. Prose that must quote a literal belongs in a .md file, which this pathspec does not cover.'

  - id: os-locations-only-via-platform
    severity: blocking
    source: '.claude/rules/node-scripts.md — Paths; adversarial review of platform-paths-and-text'
    description: 'Only lib/platform/paths.mjs asks the OS where things live; every other module and test uses the helpers'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "os\.(tmpdir|homedir)\(\)" -- "lib/*.mjs" "scripts/*.mjs" "hooks/*.mjs" "rules/*.mjs" ":!lib/platform/paths.mjs" ":!lib/platform/paths.test.mjs"'
    note: 'paths.test.mjs is the single documented exception: it asserts that the DEFAULT helpers delegate to the real OS, which cannot be asserted through the helper without becoming a tautology. Review caught two modules reading os.tmpdir() directly; this check makes the next one mechanical. KNOWN FALSE NEGATIVE, left in place deliberately and awaiting the rule owner: this pattern matches only the `os.tmpdir()` member-call spelling, so `import { tmpdir } from "node:os"` (and `require`/`await import` of the same specifier) is invisible to it. Four such violations stand today — scripts/convert-htmx-pdf.mjs:18, scripts/design-svg-logo.mjs:36, scripts/hook-cold-start.mjs:13, scripts/refine-moodboard.mjs:45 — and the check reports clean over them. Adding `-e "node:os"` fixes it, and was verified by execution to run, to report all four, and to match import/require/await-import in a probe. It is NOT applied here because this table authorises a change to edit a check only to fix a demonstrated FALSE POSITIVE; a tightening has no clause, and adding one would be a change writing its own authorisation. Found by rounds 6 and 7 of the review-housekeeping diff review; reverted in round 8. Needs /kbd-init or an explicit operator decision.'

  - id: no-zeespec
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — there is no ZeeSpec'
    description: 'No skill, hook, script or library references ZeeSpec or reads .zeespec/'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -i -e "zeespec" -- "skills/*" "lib/*" "hooks/*" "scripts/*" "templates/*"'

  - id: no-hardcoded-secrets
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md A-3; .claude/rules/docker-services.md — Compose rules'
    description: 'No inline database credentials or provider keys in code, config or Compose files'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "--(user|pass)=" -e "sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}" -- "docker/*" "*.mjs" "*.json" "*.toml" "*.yaml" "*.yml"'
    note: 'Credentials reach containers through env_file / ${VAR} from a git-ignored docker/.env. Markdown is excluded on purpose: the docs quote the source pack''s root/root as the thing not to do.'

  - id: compose-ports-loopback-only
    severity: blocking
    source: '.claude/rules/docker-services.md — Compose rules (A-3: a real boundary)'
    description: 'Every published port is bound to 127.0.0.1'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "- +.?[0-9]+:[0-9]+.? *$" -- "docker/*.yaml" "docker/*.yml"'

  - id: no-console-log-in-lib
    severity: blocking
    source: '.claude/rules/node-scripts.md — Structure (I/O lives at the edge)'
    description: 'Library modules do not print. Entry points under scripts/, hooks/ and rules/build.mjs may.'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "console\.(log|debug)" -- "lib/*.mjs" "rules/lib/*.mjs"'

  - id: no-symlinks
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — no symlinks'
    description: 'No symbolic links in the repository; installers copy; AGENTS.md is a generated copy'
    note: 'No portable one-line check exists without a forbidden tool. Manual until scripts/doctor.mjs lands (OpenSpec change installer-and-doctor); then replace this note with its command.'

  - id: exactly-two-services
    severity: blocking
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — exactly two services exist'
    description: 'docker/compose.yaml defines surrealdb, surreal-memory and liter-llm only; no other daemon, database or listening port is added'
    note: 'Manual review. A third service needs its own OpenSpec proposal that says why.'

  - id: reference-repo-untouched
    severity: blocking
    source: 'project.json workspace roles'
    description: 'Nothing under prometheus-skill-pack (the port source) is created, modified or deleted'
    note: 'Manual review of the change''s file list.'
```

## Warning constraints (acknowledge before archiving)

```yaml
  - id: tests-for-new-features
    severity: warning
    source: 'openspec/config.yaml conventions — tests written first'
    description: 'Every new module under lib/ has a node:test file that was seen to fail before it passed'

  - id: no-forbidden-tools-in-instructions
    severity: warning
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — never tell an agent to run jq, sed, grep, awk, curl, mktemp or chmod'
    description: 'SKILL.md and command files do not instruct agents to run POSIX-only tools'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "(^|[^A-Za-z])(jq|sed|awk|curl|mktemp|chmod) " -- "skills/*.md" "hooks/*" "templates/*"'
    note: 'The rule itself is blocking; the check is a heuristic and can match prose, so it is a warning that demands a human look at each hit. `grep` is left out of the pattern because `git grep` is the sanctioned replacement and would match.'

  - id: no-stub-comments
    severity: warning
    source: 'kbd generic template'
    description: 'No TODO/FIXME/STUB/HACK comments in committed code'
    check: 'git grep --no-index --exclude-standard -n -E -e "TODO|FIXME|STUB|HACK" -- "lib/*.mjs" "scripts/*.mjs" "hooks/*.mjs" "rules/*.mjs" ":!scripts/convert-htmx-react.mjs"'
    note: 'One exclusion, and it is a pathspec rather than a weakened pattern, so the rule still applies in full to every file this project authors. scripts/convert-htmx-react.mjs:308 EMITS "/* TODO: convert: ... */" into the React it generates, alongside a structured ambiguousRegions entry, so a human can see which Alpine expressions need manual rewriting. That is output data, not an unfinished stub, and deleting it would silently drop information the converter exists to surface. Proof it still discriminates: adding a real TODO comment to any other file under these pathspecs is reported.'

  - id: file-under-500-lines
    severity: warning
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — no code file over 500 lines'
    description: 'No code file exceeds 500 physical lines; partition by responsibility, never by line count'
    note: 'Manual until a Node line-count check exists. Exemptions only in rules/line-limit-allowlist.txt, and only for generated or vendored files.'

  - id: services-degrade
    severity: warning
    source: 'AGENTS.md §P — everything must still work with both services down'
    description: 'A change touching lib/memory or lib/review was exercised with the containers stopped; service-touching hooks exit 0'
    note: 'Manual. Starting Docker is tier T3 and never belongs in a workflow trigger.'

  - id: windows-verified
    severity: warning
    source: 'README §9 — open questions'
    description: 'Behaviour claimed for Windows was run on Windows, or the completion summary says it was not (A-6)'
    note: 'Until the three-OS CI matrix exists (OpenSpec change platform-foundation), every Windows claim made from macOS is self-reported.'
```

Dropped from the generic template, with reasons: `no-any-type` (no TypeScript here), `accessibility-basics`
(no UI), `no-unused-imports` and `no-lint-warnings` (no linter is configured; `lint_command` is `null` — add
them back in the change that introduces one).

## Workflow triggers

```yaml
workflow_triggers:
  - event: on_iteration_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'npm run check'

  - event: on_change_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'npm test'

  - event: on_change_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'npm run spec:validate'

  - event: on_refinement_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'git add -A'

  - event: on_refinement_complete
    action:
      type: command
      target: 'git commit -m "kbd: refine <change-id>" -m "Assisted-by: <AGENT>:<MODEL> [<tools>]"'
```

Notes on the last two: they are separate entries because of the no-chaining policy. The `Assisted-by` trailer
is required by A-15, and `Signed-off-by` must never be added. They commit locally only — nothing here pushes,
files or publishes (A-16). The repository was initialized on 2026-09-20 (`git init -b main`); it has no commits
and no remote yet, so these triggers will create the first commits and nothing can be pushed.
decision_document:
# D3 — UAR's algorithm options and where their settings live

## Decision

Every UAR option the-boss exposes must be real. Several are stubs or silent fallbacks today, so they are
implemented in UAR as part of this work, then exposed:

- skill matching `llm` (today falls back to keyword) and a real `local_embedding` (today the same code as
  `embedding`), and the unread `model_name` knob;
- the legacy intent classifier's `wasm` (errors), `llm` and `localembedding` (fall back to hybrid)
  backends, and wiring the YAML `intent_classifier` setting into the run manager (today it never reaches
  runs);
- `agentic` chunking (today falls back to document chunking).

Settings are split:

- Per agent, in a new UAR section of the agent editor (a new capability flag plus a namespaced
  `configuration.uar` object in the agent's JSON), sent inline with every run: context compaction
  strategy, skill preferences and `max_active`, tool approval and execution mode, memory and knowledge
  bases, budgets.
- App-wide, in a new `/settings/uar` page, pushed to UAR every time the-boss starts the sidecar: the
  skill-matching algorithm and thresholds, skill activation mode, guardrails, sycophancy. (UAR keeps the
  skill-matching config in memory only today, so it is lost on restart; pushing on start fixes that.)

## Assumptions

- The operator's "ALL the features it provides" means every option must actually work, not merely appear
  in a menu; showing stubs as choices would misrepresent what the product does.
- Implementing the stubs is feasible inside this effort's budget (in particular the WASM classifier and
  agentic chunking have enough design in UAR's code to finish).
- The split mirrors where UAR itself resolves each option: context strategy, tools, skills preferences,
  memory/KB and budgets resolve per run from the artifact; matching algorithm, activation mode,
  guardrails and sycophancy are global in UAR.
- Budgets in `extensions["budgets"]` are enforced on root runs (the survey only saw them read for thread
  delegation — unverified).
- Chunking is per knowledge base in UAR, so it belongs with knowledge-base settings, not per agent.

## Falsifier

This decision is wrong if:

- One or more stubs cannot be implemented to a standard where it measurably behaves differently from its
  former fallback (for example, `llm` skill matching selects the same skills as keyword matching on a
  representative evaluation set), in which case exposing it still misleads.
- Implementing the stubs costs more than the rest of the integration combined and delays a usable UAR
  runtime, with no operator-visible benefit over exposing only the working options first.
- An app-wide setting pushed at sidecar start conflicts with per-agent settings in a way the user cannot
  predict (for example, a global guardrail silently overrides a per-agent tool approval).
- Budgets turn out not to be enforced on root runs, so exposing them per agent would be a setting that
  does nothing.

original_intent:
# Operator intent (verbatim, 2026-09-22)

1. "Next, we want `the-boss` to support the universal agent runtime as an `agent runtime` like codex,
   minimax, claude code, etc. with its own configuration/settings, sidecar configuration as an embedded
   binary downloaded from a github releases setup for universal agent runtime that uses CI/CD on main
   branch to create versions for all supported platforms (windows arm/x64, macos arm/x64, linux, etc.)."
2. "In considering the universal agent runtime, that should support AG-UI as the protocol with full
   support for A2UI and its agent definitions standards, content management algorithm selection, skill
   selection algorithms, and ALL the features it provides, which may mean a slightly different subsystem
   but use deep research and adversarial review to determine the best course for all these runtimes to
   live together in the second child phase."
3. "Because we have the surreal memory server AND an instance of SurrealDB in docker, that surrealdb
   instance can be shared as a remote source by compass, UAR, and everything that needs surrealdb."

## Context the reviewer needs

- `the-boss` is an Electron app (a Cherry Studio fork). Its agent runtimes today are `claude-code`
  (Claude Agent SDK spawning the `claude` CLI), `pi` (an in-process library) and `dsh` (a Bun child
  process). Every runtime's output is converted to AI SDK v6 `UIMessageChunk` parts; the host owns model
  credentials, the system prompt, skills, memory, every MCP connection, every approval decision, and
  message persistence.
- The Universal Agent Runtime (UAR) is a Rust/Axum server with its own agent loop, 300+ providers, skill
  selection, context compaction, RAG, AG-UI streaming and A2UI v0.9.1 surfaces. It ships a sidecar
  binary (`uar-sidecar`) that binds a random loopback port and prints `READY:{port}`.
- The mini skill pack's rules require everything to keep working when the Docker services
  (surreal-memory + SurrealDB, liter-llm) are down.
